request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [Name Removed]

Gender: Male

Age: 71

Admission Date: [Date Removed]

Discharge Date: [Date Removed]

Reason for Admission:

The patient was admitted with general malaise and abnormal findings of computed tomography (CT).

Medical History:

The patient had undergone cystostomy and exchange of the catheter at regular intervals. In addition, he had a history of operation for gastric cancer with lung metastasis.

Medical Findings:

Physical examination was unremarkable. Abnormal findings of complete blood count and laboratory examination included an elevated WBC count and C-reactive protein. On the other hand, fasting blood sugar and hemoglobin A1c were within normal limits. Urinalysis showed combined hematuria and pyuria, and Escherichia coli was detected in urine culture.
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Treatment:

Due to poor condition, the patient underwent construction of the left nephrostomy. After that, remission of the inflammation was achieved, and nephrostomy catheter was also exchanged with cystostomy. Several months after the construction, the patient received left nephrectomy by open surgery. Surgical dissection was very difficult due to fixed mass. The patient received massive transfusions due to uncontrolled bleeding from frequent, extensive adhesions.

Outcome:

Unfortunately, the patient died due to sepsis and cardiovascular failure not long after the surgery.

Follow-up Care:

N/A

Signed by: [Name Removed], M.D.

Date: [Date Removed]

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
**CODE: N39**

The admission was driven by an infection of the urinary tract: elevated WBC and CRP, pyuria, and E. coli on urine culture, with the presenting malaise and CT abnormality consistent with it. The left nephrostomy was placed to manage that inflammation. The later nephrectomy and the sepsis death were consequences of the underlying process, and the gastric cancer history is a comorbidity, not the principal diagnosis.

N39 is the category for other disorders of the urinary system, which covers urinary tract infection without a more specific site or obstructive pattern. The record withholds the diagnosis section, so this is inferred from the clinical findings. If the discharge diagnosis were recorded as obstructive pyonephrosis, N13.6 would be more specific.
